title: Administrative penalty remission — Sch 1 TAA 1953
summary: This flowchart maps the administrative penalty regime under Schedule 1 to the Taxation Administration Act 1953, from the trigger provisions (s 284-75 false/misleading statements and s 284-145 scheme penalties) through base penalty calculation (s 284-90 tiers: 75% intentional disregard, 50% recklessness, 25% failure to take reasonable care; s 284-160 scheme penalties: 50% or 25%), increases for obstruction or repeat offences (s 284-220), voluntary disclosure reductions (s 284-225: 80% reduction or nil if pre-examination, 20% post-examination), and remission under s 298-20 with the PS LA 2012/5 four-step framework (correctness of penalty, circumstances of taxpayer, voluntary disclosure, exceptional circumstances). Subsection coverage: ss 284-75, 284-90, 284-145, 284-160, 284-220, 284-225, 298-20 mapped to nodes.

nodes.label: A penalty liability arises under Sch 1 TAA 1953
nodes.body: An administrative penalty under Sch 1 TAA 1953 may arise from: a false or misleading statement (s 284-75(1) — no shortfall amount required; shortfall matters only for the amount of the base penalty), an unarguable position on a taxation law (s 284-75(2)/(3)), failure to lodge or other statement defaults, or a tax avoidance scheme (s 284-145). Base penalty, increases (s 284-220), voluntary disclosure reductions (s 284-225) and remission (s 298-20) then apply.

nodes.label: What type of penalty liability?
nodes.body: Two main categories: (1) Statement or unarguable position penalty under s 284-75 (false/misleading statement, unarguable position, or failure to lodge); (2) Scheme penalty under s 284-145 (tax avoidance scheme with dominant purpose of obtaining a scheme benefit). The base penalty calculation differs between the two categories.

nodes.label: Statement / unarguable position penalty liability — s 284-75
nodes.body: Liability triggers: s 284-75(1) — statement to the Commissioner (or an entity exercising powers under a taxation law) that is false or misleading in a material particular (no shortfall required); s 284-75(2) — you treat a taxation law (incl. Income Tax, Minimum Tax and PRRT laws) as applying in a way that is not reasonably arguable and item 4, 5, 6 or 6A of the s 284-90(1) table applies; s 284-75(3) — failure to give a document/statement to the Commissioner when necessary, or where the Commissioner determines the penalty applies without the document; s 284-75(4) — statement to an entity other than the Commissioner or an entity exercising powers under a taxation law. Exceptions in s 284-75(5)-(9) (reasonable care, correction statements) are checked before the base penalty is calculated.

nodes.label: Scheme penalty liability — s 284-145
nodes.body: Liability bases under s 284-145: (1)(b)(i) sole or dominant purpose of getting a scheme benefit; (1)(b)(ia) principal purpose for Part IVA s 177DA schemes; (1)(b)(ii) principal effect for GST Div 165 schemes; (2A) scheme benefit from a determination under s 815-30 ITAA 1997 (transfer pricing) where (1)(b)(i)/(ia) not satisfied; (2B) effect given to Subdiv 815-B/815-C (amended assessment or s 128C(7) notice); (2C) other scheme benefit cases. Base penalty: 50% (or 25% reasonably arguable) for s 284-145(1)/(2C) cases; 25% (or 10% reasonably arguable) for (2A); see s 284-160(1)-(3).

nodes.label: Calculate base penalty amount — statement shortfall (s 284-90)
nodes.body: Base penalty tiers under s 284-90(1): Item 1 — intentional disregard: 75%; Item 2 — recklessness: 50%; Item 3 — failure to take reasonable care / unarguable position (other than items 6/6A): 25%; Item 4 — failure to lodge on time (statement, shortfall): 75% of the amount if it was more than 12 months late, 50% if 4-12 months, 25% if 28 days-4 months; Item 5 — failure to give other document: one base penalty unit; Item 6 — unarguable position (income tax, scheme shortfall): 25%; Item 6A — unarguable position: shortfall for a Fiscal Year exceeding the threshold under s 284-90(3A): 25% of the shortfall amount or part.

nodes.label: Calculate base penalty amount — scheme (s 284-160)
nodes.body: The base penalty for a scheme under s 284-145(1) or (2C) is: 50% of the scheme shortfall amount, or 25% if the position is reasonably arguable (s 284-160(1)). For transfer pricing schemes under s 284-145(2A): 25% of scheme shortfall amount, or 10% if reasonably arguable (s 284-160(2)). For cross-border transfer pricing under s 284-145(2B): 25% of the additional tax (s 284-160(3) table).

nodes.label: Does a penalty increase under s 284-220 apply?
nodes.body: The base penalty amount is increased by 20% for each applicable ground under s 284-220(1) (statement penalties: prevention/obstruction, becoming aware of a shortfall and not telling the Commissioner, etc.) or s 284-220(2) (scheme penalties). Increases are cumulative.

nodes.label: Apply 20% increase to the base penalty amount
nodes.body: The base penalty amount is increased by 20% for each applicable ground under s 284-220(1) (statement penalties) or s 284-220(2) (scheme penalties). The increase applies cumulatively — multiple grounds can each add 20%. The increased amount becomes the adjusted base penalty, subject to voluntary disclosure reduction and remission.

nodes.label: Apply pre-examination voluntary disclosure reduction
nodes.body: s 284-225(3): reduced by 80% if the shortfall amount (or part) is $1,000 or more; reduced to nil if less than $1,000. Scheme shortfalls: 80% (s 284-225(4)). No-shortfall false statements: nil (s 284-225(4A)).

nodes.label: Apply post-examination voluntary disclosure reduction (20%)
nodes.body: s 284-225(1): 20% reduction only if the disclosure can reasonably be estimated to have saved the Commissioner a significant amount of time or significant resources in the examination.

nodes.label: Seek remission of the penalty under s 298-20?
nodes.body: The Commissioner may remit all or part of the penalty on his own initiative or on application (s 298-20(1)). Remission is discretionary; if refused (wholly or partly), written notice and reasons must be given (s 298-20(2)). PS LA 2012/5 sets out the four-step remission framework. If no application is made, the penalty stands unless the Commissioner independently remits — that is not a refusal decision.

nodes.label: Assess remission under the PS LA 2012/5 four-step framework
nodes.body: PS LA 2012/5 sets out a four-step approach for remission: Step 1 — Is the penalty correctly imposed under the law? If not, remit to the correct amount. Step 2 — Are there circumstances of the taxpayer that warrant remission? Factors: serious illness, natural disaster, circumstances beyond the taxpayer's control, systemic ATO errors, incorrect advice from the ATO. Step 3 — Did the taxpayer make a voluntary disclosure? If so, partial remission may be appropriate beyond the statutory reduction. Step 4 — Are there exceptional circumstances justifying full or partial remission? Remission is generally only appropriate where the delay or conduct was caused by circumstances outside the taxpayer's control. Full remission is rare and usually requires exceptional circumstances.

nodes.label: Does the Commissioner grant full remission, partial remission, or refuse?
nodes.body: The Commissioner may: (a) grant full remission — penalty reduced to nil; (b) grant partial remission — penalty reduced but some amount remains payable; or (c) refuse. Written notice of the decision and reasons is required (s 298-20(2)).

nodes.label: Full remission granted — penalty reduced to nil
nodes.body: The penalty is fully remitted under s 298-20. No amount is payable. Full remission is typically granted only where the penalty was not correctly imposed or where exceptional circumstances (outside the taxpayer's control) caused the default.

nodes.label: Partial remission granted — reduced penalty payable
nodes.body: Only part of the penalty is remitted. The balance of the penalty as calculated (including any s 284-220 increase, less any s 284-225 voluntary disclosure reduction) remains payable. The Commissioner must provide written reasons for the partial remission decision (s 298-20(2)). The taxpayer may object under Part IVC if the remaining penalty exceeds 2 penalty units.

nodes.label: Remission refused — full penalty payable
nodes.body: No remission is granted. The full penalty as calculated (base penalty plus any s 284-220 increase, less any s 284-225 voluntary disclosure reduction) is payable. Written notice and reasons required (s 298-20(2)). Subject to objection under Part IVC TAA 1953.

nodes.body: The final penalty amount is determined. If the taxpayer is dissatisfied with a remission decision (or the underlying penalty assessment), they may object in the manner set out in Part IVC of the TAA 1953 within the relevant time limits. The AAT and Federal Court provide further review.

nodes.label: Does an exception in s 284-75(5)-(9) apply to the statement liability?
nodes.body: s 284-75(5): not liable if you (and your agent) took reasonable care in connection with the statement. s 284-75(6)-(7): specific statement-type exceptions. s 284-75(8): correction statements under s 389-5 (AML/CTF reporting) within the permitted period; s 284-75(9): correction statements under s 390-5. If an exception applies, no penalty.

nodes.label: No administrative penalty
nodes.body: The exception applies (or the liability basis is not made out) — no penalty under s 284-75 / s 284-145.

nodes.label: Is a purpose/effect or other liability basis in s 284-145(1)/(2A)-(2C) satisfied?
nodes.body: Bases: (1)(b)(i) sole/dominant purpose; (1)(b)(ia) principal purpose (Part IVA 177DA); (1)(b)(ii) principal effect (GST Div 165); (2A) s 815-30 transfer pricing determination; (2B) Subdiv 815-B/815-C effect; (2C) other. If none, no scheme penalty.

nodes.label: Was the voluntary disclosure before or after the examination notice?
nodes.body: Pre-examination (s 284-225(2)-(4A)) gives the larger reduction; post-examination (s 284-225(1)) gives 20% only if significant time/resources were saved. No disclosure — no reduction.

nodes.label: Pre-examination: is the shortfall amount $1,000 or more?
nodes.body: s 284-225(3): 80% reduction if $1,000 or more; reduced to nil if less than $1,000. Scheme shortfalls always 80% (s 284-225(4)).

nodes.label: Pre-examination disclosure — penalty reduced to nil (s 284-225(3)(b))
nodes.body: Shortfall (or part) is less than $1,000: the base penalty is reduced to nil.

nodes.label: Post-examination: did the disclosure save the Commissioner significant time or resources?
nodes.body: s 284-225(1)(c): the 20% post-examination reduction applies only where the disclosure can reasonably be estimated to have saved significant time or resources. If not, no reduction.

nodes.label: No remission application — penalty stands (Commissioner may still remit on own initiative)
nodes.body: s 298-20(1) permits the Commissioner to remit on his own initiative. If no application is made, the penalty remains payable unless the Commissioner independently remits — this is not a refusal decision under s 298-20(2).
